brief: TSMC hosts its 3Q26 analyst meeting on 15 October. Goldman Sachs forecasts a strong finish to 2026 with growth sustaining into 2027 as AI demand broadens across GPUs, ASICs, networking and server CPUs, with agentic AI driving a notable pickup in CPU demand. GS models 2026E/2027E revenue growth of 42.0%/36.9% YoY in USD terms, with gross margin at 67.2%/67.5%, and raises 2027E/2028E capex forecasts to $85bn/$98bn from $78bn/$82bn to support further capacity expansion. Within the near term, GS expects 3Q26E revenue to grow 15.3% QoQ and 4Q26E a further 11.0% QoQ, with GM dipping to 67.5%/67.3% versus 67.7% in 2Q26 on N2 ramp dilution. At its Communacopia conference, TSMC management said lower token costs should spur greater AI consumption and that customer/CSP discussions reinforce demand confidence, while N2/N3 supply should stay insufficient despite expansion. GS raised 2026/27/28E earnings estimates 1%/7%/8% and raised its 12-month price target to NT$3,300 (ADR $660) from NT$3,100 ($620), implying 28% (ADR 40%) upside; it reiterates Buy.
